title: Call utils and stats functions with their namespace
description:
Fixes #5. Should also fix mlverse/torch#1463.

Related: mlverse/torch#1478 makes torch warn and keep loading when `lib_path()` errors, instead of reporting that torch failed to start. That guards against the symptom, and this PR fixes the cause.

`lib_path()`, `cuda_path()` and `.read_components()` call `packageName()`, `read.delim()` and `setNames()` without importing utils or stats. When no default packages are attached, every exported path function errors with "could not find function packageName". R CMD INSTALL and R CMD check run R that way. torch calls `lib_path()` at startup, so with cuda12.8 installed it can't preload the CUDA libraries and fails to start, and any package that loads torch fails R CMD check.

The change qualifies the calls with `utils::` and `stats::`, adds `Imports: stats, utils` to the DESCRIPTION template, and runs sync.sh to update all four cuda* packages.

Checked with cuda12.8 installed with `CUDA_COMPONENTS=runtime`:

- With `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL`, `lib_path()`, `cuda_path()`, `include_path()` and `all_lib_paths()` all error on main and return the expected paths with this change.
- With `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL`, `loadNamespace("torch")` fails on main with "could not find function packageName". With this change torch starts and maps `libcudart.so.12` from the cuda12.8 lib directory.
- R CMD check no longer gives the "no visible global function definition" NOTE for these calls. The missing-documentation WARNING is unchanged, since the packages ship no man pages.

I left `PKG_VERSION` alone. Installs that already have 1.0.9 will need a version bump to pick this up through `update.packages()`.

title: Add SystemRequirements for Linux/Windows-only support
description:
## Summary
- Adds `SystemRequirements: Linux or Windows; not supported on macOS.` to all package DESCRIPTION files and the shared template.
- Documents the OS restriction already enforced by the configure script.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify DESCRIPTION files render correctly on CRAN-like checks

title: Add CUDA 12.9 support
description:
## Summary
- Add `cuda12.9` package (toolkit 12.9.1, cuDNN 9.20.0.48, NCCL 2.29.7, NVSHMEM 3.6.5)
- Add `cuda12.9` to CI test matrix

## Test plan
- [ ] CI passes for `cuda12.9` in the test-install workflow
